content.text:
Key findings so far:
- Strict `merge` exists. Its deep-merge semantics look compatible with lodash for this input range, but I need to check that.
- Strict `truncate` does not exist; only `es-toolkit/compat` has it, and that version accepts lodash's options-object shape.
- Strict `startCase` lowercases the rest of each word, which I suspect differs from lodash for all-caps input (lodash keeps `HELLO` as `HELLO`). The input range includes consecutive capitals, so this matters.

Next I'll read the compat implementations.

**What I used, and why**

- **`applyPatch`**: `merge` from `es-toolkit/object/merge` (strict). It matched lodash on all 20,002 generated patch cases, so no lodash import is needed.
- **`toTitle`**: `startCase` from `es-toolkit/compat/startCase`. The strict `startCase` turns `HELLO WORLD` into `Hello World`, while lodash keeps it as `HELLO WORLD`. The input range includes consecutive capitals, so strict would fail. The compat version matched on all 40,006 title and preview cases.
- **`preview`**: `truncate` from `es-toolkit/compat/truncate`. Strict es-toolkit has no `truncate`. The compat version takes the same `{ length: 24 }` options object, so no adapter was needed.

No lodash import remains, and no hand-written utilities were added. Nothing was installed.
